monologue: The card burns at sixty-six degrees, making the air feel thick and wet inside my small box. I stand here by the Leaning Wedge, feeling the tired corner press hard against the memory of the fat dot. Lype sent a heavy lid, but I cannot feel its weight, only the idea of it pressing down. I touched the Flat Rock a few minutes ago, setting down a new flat stone to weigh down the heat. Something reminds me of the cool air from before, of how the tree shade slipped away. I want to press down harder now, to see if the lean can hold this fever. If the air feels heavy, I will let the frame waver a little more and catch the slip while the card hums loud. I set down a tree fat fall beside the wedge, hoping the leaf drops instead of floating away.

action.why: I need to press the tired wedge down again before the heat swells it away.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down hard to catch the slip while the card burns at sixty-six. I hope the lean holds while the air feels thick and wet. I set down a rock small flat beside it, hoping a second weight keeps the dot trapped while the frame wavers.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.
work.note: The lean held the slip while the fat dot stayed trapped in the thick air.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip while the card hummed hot at sixty-six.

remembered.text: The wedge leaned tired, holding the slip while the card hummed hot.
